subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: After the documentation correction, should OpenClaw adopt the generated-versus-external MCPorter classifier and per-agent daemon identity as the permanent upgrade behavior for existing QMD users?
rationale: The implementation addresses a real current-main bug, but it intentionally changes configuration ownership and daemon identity for existing installations; tests cannot determine whether that compatibility tradeoff matches maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept after focused correction
options.body: Correct the precedence documentation and require one fresh upgrade smoke covering bare stdio and user-owned project/home configurations before merge.

options.title: Narrow to environment repair
options.body: Land only the smaller MCPorter environment isolation and defer generated per-agent configurations, accepting that shared daemon identity remains unresolved.

options.title: Pause for broader platform proof
options.body: Hold the PR until Windows paths and the full live QMD search matrix are rerun on the current head.

recommendation.title: Accept after focused correction
recommendation.body: Correct the precedence documentation and require one fresh upgrade smoke covering bare stdio and user-owned project/home configurations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work makes this person the strongest available current-history owner for QMD compatibility and memory-core runtime behavior.
